en.title: Goldman Sachs OA #32: Threshold Alerts
en.description:
A compliance system monitors call volume. Whenever the average call volume over the most recent few minutes exceeds a threshold, it raises an alert. Let precedingMinutes=k. At time T (counting from 1), take the call volumes at the k times T−(k−1), T−(k−2), …, T and compute their average; raise one alert if the average is strictly greater than alertThreshold. When T<k there is not enough data, and no alert is raised.

Given the call volume of each minute, find the total number of alerts raised over the whole period.
en.input: The first line contains precedingMinutes; the second line alertThreshold; the third line n; then n lines, each containing an integer numCalls[i], the call volume in minute i+1. 1≤precedingMinutes≤n, 1≤alertThreshold≤10^5, 1≤n≤10^5, 0≤numCalls[i]≤10^5.
en.output: Output one integer, the total number of alerts.
en.explanation:
Example 1: k=3, threshold 4, numCalls=[2,2,2,2,5,5,5,8]. At T=3 the average is (2+2+2)/3=2; the averages for T=4..8 are 2,3,4,5,6 in turn, and the last two exceed 4, for 2 alerts in total (an average equal to 4 raises no alert).
Example 2: k=2, threshold 3; the averages are 3.5,3.5,3 in turn, and the first two exceed 3, for 2 alerts.
Example 3: with k=1 it is simply a minute-by-minute comparison; 6 and 7 exceed 5, for 2 alerts.
hints: The window is only complete once T reaches k.
The average is a real number; when comparing, you can multiply both sides of the inequality by k.
Maintain the sum of the most recent k minutes with a sliding window.
